mergeContract.rule: Compare dates per FIELD, not per quest. Keep whichever value is newer.
mergeContract.undated: dating:"none" means the source cannot say when the value was last true. Never let an undated value overwrite a dated one, in either direction.
precedence: observed (the game itself) outranks everything, whatever the dates say
otherwise the newer date wins, and a dated value beats an undated one
mergeContract.devDating: tarkov.dev publishes no per-task date, so a value of its carries one ONLY when this repo watched it change between builds: dating:"observed-change", asOf = the day it moved. That is evidence it is at least that new, not a claim about when the game changed. A value never seen to move stays dating:"none".
mergeContract.quickCheck: Each quest carries a top-level `asOf`, the newest of its field dates. If yours is newer than that, you can skip the whole record.

observed.what: Read off the in-game quest screen and transcribed.
observed.datingNote: The day the quest was seen on screen.
observed.license: CC0-1.0, this is our own observation, use it freely.

wiki.datingNote: The page's last revision timestamp, per quest.
wiki.license: CC BY-SA 3.0, attribution and share-alike apply to anything derived from it.
wiki.attribution: Escape from Tarkov Wiki contributors, https://escapefromtarkov.fandom.com

overlay.what: tarkov-data-overlay (tarkovtracker-org), a correction layer over tarkov.dev.
overlay.datingNote: One build date for the whole file ($meta.generated); it cannot date a single task.

tarkov.dev.what: json.tarkov.dev, the widest coverage, and the only source with map coordinates.
tarkov.dev.datingNote: PUBLISHES NO DATE FOR A TASK, at any granularity. `asOf` is null on purpose: the fetch time says when we downloaded it, not when the record was last true. Never let an undated value overwrite a dated one.
